reason: Task interpretation is typically followed by an environment scan so the agent can ground the parsed subgoals in visible objects and receptacles.
The interpreted goal provides the destinations and search priorities that the navigation planner turns into movement decisions.
The planner decides where to go next, and the location navigator executes that movement.
Receptacle navigation is a specific case of the broader location-navigation capability.
Appliance navigation is a specialized form of moving to a target location.
Systematic search execution relies on a planner to sequence candidate locations and traverse them efficiently.
Search verification usually follows an initial systematic search to double-check missed or ambiguous locations.
The object locator proposes likely locations, and the target-object locator navigates there to confirm the object.
Confirming a target object's location requires physically reaching the suspected location.
The tool must be found before it can be used on a target object.
Both skills search for a suitable receptacle, differing mainly in search breadth and search strategy.
Storage exploration is a narrower version of receptacle searching focused on drawers, cabinets, and other storage units.
After finding a suitable receptacle, the agent typically needs to verify and prepare it for placement.
Both skills open a closed receptacle to expose its contents for further interaction.
Opening a receptacle is one branch of the broader receptacle-operator skill.
Closing a receptacle is the complementary branch of the broader receptacle-operator skill.
Preparing a receptacle usually requires deciding whether to open or close it before use.
Appliance preparation is a specialized form of receptacle preparation for microwaves, fridges, and similar stations.
An appliance must first be reached before it can be prepared for use.
Both acquire an object into inventory once its location is known.
After retrieving an object, inventory tracking helps maintain counts and decide what still needs to be found.
Transporting an object requires first acquiring it from the source receptacle.
Transport naturally culminates in placing the carried object at the destination.
Successful placement depends on the destination receptacle being accessible and ready.
Storage is a specific object-placement scenario focused on placing an item into a validated storage location.
Disposal is a specific case of placing an object into a garbage or discard receptacle.
State inspection produces evidence that the task verifier uses to judge whether the goal has been satisfied.
Task verification often needs inventory state to determine whether all required objects have been collected or placed.
Temperature regulation is a specialized subclass of object state modification.
Heating is one specific temperature-regulation operation.
Cooling is the complementary temperature-regulation operation.
Heating with a named appliance is a narrower version of the generic object-heating skill.
Cleaning is a specific type of state modification focused on cleanliness.
Changing object state with an appliance usually requires the appliance to be prepared first.
State modification is commonly paired with state inspection to verify whether the desired state has been reached.
Cooling an object requires a reachable, ready cooling appliance such as a fridge.
Heating with an appliance requires the appliance to be in the right open or closed state first.
Cleaning often depends on preparing the sink or other cleaning receptacle for use.
Both skills use a tool or device to act on a target object, differing mainly in the type of instrument being used.
Before operating a device on an object, the agent often needs to find that device in the environment.
Searching for a receptacle requires moving between candidate receptacle locations.
Once likely object locations are hypothesized, the search-pattern executor can traverse them systematically.
Once the target object is visually confirmed, the next step is usually to retrieve it.
The initial scan provides the set of visible receptacles and objects that a systematic search will iterate through.
Storing an object usually starts with finding a suitable target receptacle.
Disposal often begins by locating a garbage or other valid disposal receptacle.
